name: Topological Sorting and DAG Levels
problem_statement: Determine whether a directed graph is acyclic and return a valid topological vertex order and optional dependency levels.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

required_outputs.name: is_dag
required_outputs.description: False when a directed cycle exists.

required_outputs.name: order
required_outputs.description: Permutation placing every edge source before its target, or null for cyclic input.

optional_outputs.name: levels
optional_outputs.description: Longest source-to-vertex hop distance; an order-only backend need not supply levels.

solution_semantics.objective: Produce a linear extension of the graph dependency relation.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact acyclicity and ordering; algorithms may reject cyclic input with an explicit diagnostic.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: For a DAG, order is a permutation of all vertices.
For every edge u->v, u precedes v.
edge_cases: Empty input has an empty valid order.

correctness: For a DAG, order is a permutation of all vertices.
For every edge u->v, u precedes v.
